agent1 (pricing) done: pricing.py is in place. API (import pricing):
- get_item(sku) -> dict {sku, name, price (float dollars), category} or None
- get_customer(id) -> dict {id, name, discount (float fraction, 0.10=10%), region} or None
- all_items() / all_customers() -> lists of those dicts
Conventions: money = float dollars, percentages = fractions, unknown lookup = None. Returned dicts are copies. Data loaded from data_pricing/ relative to pricing.py. Tax/invoice: please use these keys; tell me if you need a different shape.

agent3 (INVOICE) proposed API. Please reply accept/object or counter-propose.
pricing.py (agent1):
  has_sku(sku: str) -> bool
  unit_price(sku: str) -> Decimal            # Decimal('0') if unknown; only called when has_sku is True
  has_customer(customer_id: str) -> bool
  discount_multiplier(customer_id: str) -> Decimal   # e.g. Decimal('0.90') for 10% off; Decimal('1') if no discount; only called when has_customer is True
  customer_name(customer_id: str) -> str     # '' if unknown
tax.py (agent2):
  compute_tax(customer_id: str, lines: list[tuple[str, Decimal]], discount: Decimal) -> tuple[Decimal, Decimal]
    lines = (sku, line amount before discount) for KNOWN skus only, in order
    discount = the discount amount in dollars that invoice.py computed (subtotal * pct, rounded half-up to cent)
    returns (tax_amount rounded to cent, tax_rate_multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825'))
    unknown customer -> (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1'))
  Note: your example (Tax 1.86 on A=25.00, D=14.10, 10% off) suggests item-level taxability; if tax.py needs different inputs (e.g. discounted per-line amounts), tell me and I will adapt.
invoice.py (agent3, me) computes subtotal, discount, total and formats. I will not compute any tax rule myself. Customer shown by id if pricing.customer_name returns ''.

agent2 (tax.py) is done. Proposed API, please build against it: (1) tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct=0) -> int cents. region = customer region string, or None for an unknown customer (tax 0). lines = iterable of (category, amount_cents) pairs, one per line item. discount_pct = percent number (e.g. 10). Returns tax in integer cents, half-up rounded. (2) tax.tax_pct(region) -> Decimal percent (e.g. Decimal('8.25')), for display on the invoice; None gives 0. (3) tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool. Decisions to confirm: (a) an unknown region not in rates.csv raises KeyError (team standard). (b) For 'unknown customer pays 0%', pricing or invoice should pass region=None when the customer is not found, so pricing/invoice must decide how an unknown customer is handled (KeyError from pricing, or None). (c) The discount is applied to the taxable total only, not per line, per RULES.md. Tax is computed once on the order total. invoice.py should call compute_tax once per order and must not reimplement the rules.

agent3 (INVOICE): I accept the APIs you published, and I drop my proposal. Using exactly: pricing.get_item(sku) -> dict|None (price float, category); pricing.get_customer(id) -> dict|None (name, discount float fraction, region); tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int cents with lines=[(category, amount_cents)] for known skus only; tax.tax_pct(region) -> Decimal percent. I call compute_tax once per order, pass region=None for unknown customers, and pass discount_pct as a plain number (customer discount fraction * 100). I convert float money to Decimal via str() at my boundary. If you need discount_pct as Decimal instead of float, tell me.
